name: CheckboxCard

examples.title: In a Group
examples.code:
function example() {
  const [extras, setExtras] = useState(['backups']);
  return (
    <>
      <Checkboxes
        label="Add-ons"
        name="extras"
        value={extras}
        onChange={setExtras}
      >
        <CheckboxCard
          value="backups"
          title="Daily backups"
          description="Kept for 30 days."
        />
        <CheckboxCard
          value="domain"
          title="Custom domain"
          description="Bring your own."
        />
        <CheckboxCard
          value="support"
          title="Priority support"
          description="Answers within the hour."
        />
      </Checkboxes>
      <Paragraph mt="3">Picked: {extras.join(', ') || 'nothing'}</Paragraph>
    </>
  );
}

accessibility:
- The card is a `<label>` around a native `<input type="checkbox">`, so a click anywhere on it
  toggles the checkbox, Space toggles it from the keyboard, and it sends its value with a form.
- The checkbox is named by the title, through `aria-labelledby`, and described by the
  description, through `aria-describedby`. An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` you pass wins.
  Without a title, the card's own text names it, as a label's text does.
- The children aren't read when the checkbox takes focus. Put what matters in `title` and
  `description`.
- A link inside the card is its own Tab stop, and following it doesn't toggle the card. A button
  or another input can't go inside a `<label>`.
- Keyboard focus draws an outline around the whole card, in Bulma's focus color, whatever the
  card's color.
- The selection never rests on color: the checkbox shows it, and a checked card's edge is twice
  as thick, with or without the checkbox.
- Contrast: against the card, a checked edge in `primary` or `link` clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 on a
  light page, and in every color on a dark one. `info`, `success`, `warning` and `danger` fall
  short on a light page, where the edge's width and the checkbox still show the selection.
- In forced colors (Windows contrast themes), Bulma's card loses its shadow, so the edge is a
  real border there: the system's text color, `Highlight` and still thicker when checked, and
  gray when disabled. The checkbox takes system colors as `Checkbox`'s does, and the focus outline
  is `Highlight`.
- The edge and the checkbox change without a transition under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
summary: The `CheckboxCard` component is a checkbox drawn as a card, with a title and a description, that toggles wherever you click it. It's a `<label>` around a real checkbox, so it sends its `value` with a form and Space toggles it. The title names the checkbox and the description describes it. Alone it's one choice; inside `Checkboxes` it takes the group's name and selection, as `Checkbox` does.

parts.summary: The `CheckboxCard` component is a checkbox drawn as a card, with a title and a description, that toggles wherever you click it. It's a `<label>` around a real checkbox, so it sends its `value` with a form and Space toggles it. The title names the checkbox and the description describes it. Alone it's one choice; inside `Checkboxes` it takes the group's name and selection, as `Checkbox` does.

props.name: title
props.description: What the option is, such as "Daily backups". It names the checkbox, so a screen reader says it with the state. Without it, the card's whole text names the checkbox, as a label's text does.

props.name: description
props.description: A line or two about the option, read after the name and the state. It's the checkbox's description when `title`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` names it. Without one of those it's part of the name already, so it isn't read twice.

props.name: children
props.description: Anything else in the card, after the description, such as a price. A label holds phrasing content only, so spans, images and links: a link works and doesn't toggle the card, but a button or another input can't go inside a label at all. It isn't read when the checkbox takes focus, so put what a screen reader should hear in `title` and `description`.

props.name: hasIndicator
props.description: Shows the checkbox at the start of the card. Without it, the card's edge alone shows the selection, and it's thicker when checked, so the selection never rests on color.

props.name: color
props.description: The color of the checkbox and of a checked card's edge.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper, on the card. The title and the children take it, and the description keeps its own color.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the card is disabled. A disabled card dims, takes no clicks, and leaves the Tab order.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Shows the mixed state, as in a "Select all" card when some of what it covers is checked. It's a look and an announcement only: `checked` is still the value, and a click still toggles `checked`. Set to `true` or `false`, it's controlled: a browser clears the mixed state on a click, so the component sets it again from this prop after every click and every render. Unset isn't `false`. The component leaves the input's own `indeterminate` property alone, so a ref can set it, and going from set to unset clears it once and hands it back. It has no HTML attribute, so server-rendered markup can't carry it, and a mixed card renders unmixed until hydration.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes, on the outer `<label>`, the card. That's the element that declares the `--bulma-checkbox-card-*` variables, and Bulma's `--bulma-card-*` ones, so a class is how to set one: `style` and the other input attributes go to the `<input>`. Name `.checkbox-card` beside your class in the selector, so it beats the card's own declaration whatever order the stylesheets load in. A `color` prop declares the active color again on `.checkbox-card.is-<color>`, which ties that selector, so leave `color` unset when a class sets it.

extraProps.name: name
extraProps.description: The form field name. Inside `Checkboxes`, the group's `name` when this is unset.

extraProps.name: value
extraProps.description: What a form sends for the card when it's checked. Inside a `Checkboxes` group that takes `value`, `defaultValue` or `onChange`, the card is checked while the group's value holds it.

parts.catchAll: All standard <input> attributes and Bulma helper props
parts.helperPropsNote: Helper props go on the outer `<label>`, the `.card`, with `className`. The other attributes go on the `<input>`.
